status: Untested in-game. No dotnet on this Linux VM; client is net48/Windows-only. First live test is the watcher log + 2-player vote test in CUTSCENE_VOTE_V2.md.

confidenceLevels.cross-checked: Cutscene name seen in the decompiled mission script AND in DurtyFree cutsceneNames.json AND the autosplitter label agrees.
confidenceLevels.verified: Cutscene name seen in the decompiled mission script AND in DurtyFree cutsceneNames.json.
confidenceLevels.script-only: Cutscene name seen in the decompiled mission script but NOT in cutsceneNames.json. Do not use for playback until verified in-game.

fieldNotes.name: Canonical cutscene name, lowercase — what REQUEST_CUTSCENE wants. Cutscene names are case-insensitive in the game; nameAsInScript keeps the script's original case.
fieldNotes.actors: Cutscene entity handle strings from REGISTER_ENTITY_FOR_CUTSCENE in the mission script. These are the scene's internal handle names (e.g. 'Lamar', 'Jimmys_Car'), NOT ped model names. actorsScope 'per-cutscene' means the handles were in the same function that requests this scene; 'mission-level' means they were seen in the script but could not be attributed to one scene. null means no handles were found for this scene.
fieldNotes.origin: World XYZ the cutscene plays from. Always null in v1 of this map — no fetched source carries it (fivemad's browser is a JS app with no data in the fetched HTML). Fill from the CutsceneWatcher log (player position when the cutscene fires) or from fivemad manually.
fieldNotes.durationMs: Always null in v1 — same reason as origin. Fill from the watcher log (start/end GameTime) or fivemad.
fieldNotes.playbackLists: REQUEST_CUTSCENE_WITH_PLAYBACK_LIST indices seen in the script, verbatim. null means the script only ever requests the scene plain (flags 8).
fieldNotes.flagsSeen: Flags argument seen on REQUEST_CUTSCENE calls for this scene (usually 8).

sources.decompiled-script: Sainan/GTA-V-Decompiled-Scripts (master, fetched 2026-11-21) — decompiled_scripts/<missionScript>.c; ground truth for which cutscenes a mission requests.
sources.autosplitter: hoXyy/GTAV-AutoSplitter GTAV-Auto-Splitter.asl (fetched 2026-11-21) — vars.missions (mission IDs) and vars.cutsceneNames (cutscene -> mission-segment labels).
sources.cutsceneNames.json: DurtyFree/gta-v-data-dumps cutsceneNames.json (fetched 2026-11-21) — 807 entries, 772 unique names; used only to confirm a name exists in the game files.
sources.gta-wiki: GTA Wiki, Missions in GTA V (gta.fandom.com/wiki/Missions_in_GTA_V, read 2026-11-21) — mission order, descriptions, protagonists.
sources.fivemad: fivemad Cutscene Browser (fivemad.com/docs/tools/cutscenes) — cited as the manual lookup for actors / length / world position; its pages are a JS app and carry no cutscene data in the fetched HTML, so nothing from it is in this map.
